News.title: Glam JPMorgan executive ‘drugged and abused married junior employee’ as she ‘made him her office sex slave’
News.content:
‘I OWN YOU' Glam JPMorgan executive ‘drugged and abused married junior employee’ as she ‘made him her office sex slave’

A SENIOR JPMorgan executive has been accused of sexually assaulting, racially abusing and drugging a junior employee across several months.

Lorna Hajdini, 37, allegedly coerced a married banker into “non-consensual and humiliating sex acts” and threatened his career when he refused her advances, according to a lawsuit.





The accuser, known only as John Doe, claims he was even verbally abused by Hajdini after he broke down in tears during one of the alleged unwanted sexual encounters.

Hajdini, an executive director in JPMorgan Chase’s Leveraged Finance division, allegedly also admitted to drugging Doe with a date rape drug on multiple occasions.

The lawsuit also claims Doe was given “an erection-enabling pharmaceutical substance”.

Hajdini, who has worked for the company for almost 15 years, is yet to respond to the allegations.



Doe joined as a Senior VP/Director in March 2024 and claims the alleged abuse started almost immediately after Hajdini was appointed to the team in a senior role in April.

One of the first claims in the New York suit comes from May 2024, as Doe alleges Hajdini dropped a pen on the floor next to his desk and then rubbed his leg and squeezed his calf as she picked it up.



He accuses her of then saying to him: “Oh, you did play basketball in college?

“I love basketball players… they get me so wet.”

The concerning advances quickly ramped up, Doe claims.

Weeks later, Doe says Hajdini invited him out for drinks to which he quickly declined.

She allegedly issued a chilling response, saying: “If you don’t f**k me soon, I’m going to ruin you.



“Never forget, I f**king own you.”

Doe claims he continued to reject any of the offers to meet outside of work but says the abuse only got worse – even turning racially driven, according to the lawsuit.

Hajdini allegedly asked to give him oral sex in the office as the legal filings claim she said: “Birthday BJ for the brown boy? My little brown boy.”

Doe accuses Hajdini of repeatedly groping him around his groin at a work social event and spitting in her hands before rubbing it over his neck and head.

The suit alleges Hajdini said during the same event: “You’re gonna need to earn it, my little Arab boy toy.”



Doe also claims Hajdini used her executive status to gain unauthorised access to all his bank accounts.

This allowed her to track his “every move”, the suit claims.

In one alleged instance, Doe alleges Hajdini turned up to his apartment, took off her top and started touching her breasts in front of him.

He claims he again rejected her advances before she starting to verbally attack him and his wife.

Doe accuses her of saying: “Do you want to get promoted at year end or not?



“Do you want a future at JPMorgan? It’s that simple. I don’t know why you’re fighting this.”

Before allegedly adding: “I bet your little Asian, fish head, wife doesn’t have these cannons.”

Moments later, Doe accuses his superior of forcibly removing his pants and performing oral sex on him against his will.

He says he started to cry and was again verbally abused, according to the suit.

“Stop f**king crying. You think anyone would ever believe you? You’re a f**king douche bag who thinks he’s hot s**t.



“But you can’t even get your d**k hard for me? What the f**k is this?” the lawsuit alleges Hajdini said.

He claims he was then forced to perform oral sex on the accused out of “embarrassment and humiliation”, according to the legal filings.

In the same month, Doe alleges he was assaulted again.

During the alleged encounter, Doe claims he said: “I’m very uncomfortable, please, Lorna, please, I’m begging you.”

A witness is cited in the complaint as overhearing the alleged sexual abuse taking place as they were staying in the adjoining room.



Over the following months, Doe claims Hajdini continued to subject him to sexual advances at work and in public.

The complaint says the exec repeatedly reminded him that she “owned” and could control his bonuses, promotions and future work relationships.

The Sun has contacted Hajdini for comment.

In May 2025, Doe delivered a written complaint to JPMorgan’s HR team detailing what he described as race and gender-based discrimination, harassment and a pattern of “severe sexual abuse”.

He claims the firm didn’t immediately respond but alleges they started retaliating against him.



The suit sees him allege he was sent anonymous threatening phone calls from individuals he believes were acting on behalf of Hajdini and others in the company.

One caller allegedly told him: “Just wait ‘till you’re back in New York, Brown boy.

“You better stay away – snitch.”

On June 9, 2025, Doe says he received a voicemail from someone claiming to be a manager at the company, telling him he wasn’t welcome back because of his skin color.

Another caller allegedly threatened to contact US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) about him and his family.



He was later reprimanded and locked out of all company systems and placed on involuntary leave.

JPMorgan Chase has denied Doe’s claims saying an investigation found no evidence to support his allegations.

Hajdini is still employed at the company but Doe left in late 2024.

Doe is now seeking damages for lost earnings, emotional distress and reputational harm, according to the complaint.

A spokesman for JPMorgan Chase said in a statement to the Daily Mail: “Following an investigation, we don’t believe there’s any merit to these claims.

“While numerous employees cooperated with the investigation, the complainant refused to participate and has declined to provide facts that would be central to support his allegations.”

News.title: Morrisons worker, 62, sacked after 30 years for tackling teenage shoplifter and ‘putting company reputation in jeopardy’
News.content:
BASKET BRAWL Morrisons worker, 62, sacked after 30 years for tackling teenage shoplifter and ‘putting company reputation in jeopardy’

A LOYAL Morrisons worker with 30 years of service has been sacked after tackling a teenage shoplifter.

Karate-trained Jane Pilborough, 62, saw her three-decade career ended because bosses claimed she put the supermarket’s reputation “in jeopardy” by ignoring their “deter-not-detain” policy.





The grandmother claims she was the only staff member to step up and try to stop a young thief smuggling “chicken bites” out of the Newark store in his pockets.

Despite her unblemished record, the grandmother found herself out of a job after the confrontation in Nottinghamshire turned into what she described as a “tug of war”.

CCTV footage showed her falling to the ground as the shoplifter spun around to shake her off before fleeing.

And she believed he was 18, it later emerged he was just 14 or 15.

Shaken Ms Pilborough was left with minor injuries to her hand and knee, but instead of being hailed a hero, she was hauled into a disciplinary meeting in August 2024.

By the end of the month, the grandmother was sacked for gross misconduct.

She told the Daily Mail the move left her feeling like she had been dumped on the “scrapheap”.

“I still feel resentful of the way I was treated,” she told the outlet.



Ms Pilborough claimed she was put in an “impossible situation” after a manager called over headsets for the thief to be stopped and the doors blocked.

She added: “Security didn’t respond.

“I found myself in an impossible situation where I saw the individual just walk straight through one of the checkouts past the last point of payment.”

Ms Pilborough insisted she followed rules by trying to persuade the lad to pay for the hot food.

But as he neared the exit, the yob “made a sudden move,” and the retail worker grabbed his rucksack in what she called “natural instinct”.



The acting team leader said she had no memory of the scuffle as she went into “fight or flight mode”, reports the Mail Online.

During the investigation, she told bosses she felt her “automatic response and karate training [had] gone against me”.

A dismissal letter told her: “Your actions put yourself in danger, the lives of your fellow colleagues and other customers.”

It added that her actions could have been “filmed and shared on social media at any point”.

Bosses even suggested she could have faced criminal charges for touching a juvenile.



An appeal was rejected in October 2024.

While bosses called her care for the store “admirable,” they said the situation could have been de-escalated by “simply letting the shoplifter leave”.

Morrisons‘ policy, introduced in 2023, reportedly suggests staff offer thieves a basket rather than challenging them.

However, disciplinary notes of Ms Pilborough’s case make reference to her being “past the point of offering a basket”.

Ms Pilborough, who has since found another job, remains bitter, claiming the company has decided on a “hard line” to dismiss anyone who gets involved.



A spokesperson for Morrisons said: “We recognise that difficult situations like this can cause real challenges for colleagues in store.

“That’s why, when dealing with a shoplifter, a colleague’s safety is always the number one priority and why we have clear procedures in place to de-escalate incidents, to prevent any of our colleagues being put at risk in a physical struggle and coming to harm.

“We believe colleague safety always outweighs the protection of stock. We cannot ignore the potential for violence, and it is essential to remember that only the police are authorised to intervene in these situations.

“Unfortunately, the former colleague’s actions and the evidence to the disciplinary hearing showed that, although she had been trained on how to respond to a theft situation safely just a few weeks before the incident, she did not follow that procedure and that led to a physical altercation with a juvenile shoplifter.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The matter was investigated thoroughly and, regretfully, the recommendation of the disciplinary panel was that she be dismissed.



“This was upheld on appeal.”

News.title: Where was Rachel? Timeline of Brit influencer’s mystery disappearance in Morocco including missed flight & 5am club exit
News.content:
RACHEL Kerr vanished on an ill-fated work trip to Morocco – sparking a desperate search among her “extremely worried” family and friends.

Travel influencer Rachel, 31, suddenly vanished without a trace before being found safe in an apartment just five days later after “voluntarily” checking out of her hotel and cutting off contact with loved ones.





During the whirlwind hunt for Rachel which started last weekend, a friend claimed the Brit had refused to board a plane home and instead extended her stay in Morocco weeks earlier.

She was also said to have run out of money on the same day she ventured out to a local nightclub where she was last seen by friends at around 5am.

Using Rachael’s social media and statements by those who know her, The Sun has now constructed a timeline around Kerr’s disappearance and her being found on Wednesday in the coastal city of Agadir.

Rachel landed in Agadir Al-Massira International Airport in southwest Morocco on March 30 after a four-hour flight from Scotland where she lives.



She shared dozens of videos and pictures to her TikTok and Instagram shortly after landing which included snaps of her hotel – the Caribbean Village.

Rachel said she was staying in Morocco to escape her hometown of Dunblane, Scotland, and to “get some sun in my body”.



Days later, she posted a video of the city with the caption: “What a life to be able to wander about and explore places on our planet, meet new people and learn new things.”

During her time away, Rachel is believed to have travelled to multiple cities in Morocco but always returned to Agadir after a day or two of exploring.

Several vlogs were uploaded to her Instagram up until mid-April detailing these new adventures to her nearly 10,000 followers.



Posted alongside these videos included a range of bikini snaps and clips of her dancing.

Close friend Alexis Shaw, who was helping with the search, says that on around April 10, Rachel was due to fly home.

But she refused to return to the UK and instead extended her stay – despite her family trying to bring her back.



Then on April 13, Rachel posted for the final time before vanishing on her social media.

She shared two glamorous pictures of her posed up on a hotel bed alongside the caption “la marina”.

Her Instagram, which is often flooded with posts and stories every day, has now been dormant for over two weeks.

Despite her social media silence, Rachel was still hanging out with her friends out in Agadir.



Rachel’s brother is even known to have entered Morocco on April 22 before leaving the country after a few days of trying to convince her to come home.

Speaking on Tuesday, pal Alexis said: “She [Rachel] was due to fly home a couple of weeks ago and her brother flew out to find her.

“Her brother had to leave and came home after a few days for work and she was refusing to come home.”

Alexis also revealed that on April 24, Rachel had started to worry after “running out of money”.



Timeline of Rachel Kerr's disappearance March 30 – Rachel lands in Agadir, Morocco after catching a flight from Scotland Around April 10 – Rachel is due to fly home but extends her stay in Agadir April 13 – Her final social media post is made on Instagram of her in a hotel room April 22 – Rachel’s brother enters Morocco before leaving a few days later April 24 – Friend says Rachel has ‘run out of money’ April 24 – Rachel goes to SMART NightClub overnight April 25 – Influencer is seen leaving the club at 5am Hours later – Rachel checks out of her hotel and turns off her phone April 27 – Moroccan police open up investigation into Rachel’s disappearance April 28 – News of her disappearance becomes public in UK media April 29 – Concerned loved ones fly to Agadir to help with the search April 29 – Police announce they have found her in an apartment in the city

She said the Brit appeared to be “in mental crisis and a danger to herself” but the social media star still didn’t want to come home.

Instead, that same evening she headed out to a popular nightclub just two minutes away from the hotel.

Rachel went to the SMART NightClub, described online as a high-energy popular dance venue, and stayed until the early hours of the morning.

She was last seen by friends leaving the club on April 25, at around 5am.



Rachel is then known to have checked out of the Caribbean Village hotel and left the complex.

Almost immediately, she turned off her phone and was unable to be contacted, her concerned loved ones said.

Moroccan police announced they had opened up an investigation into Rachel’s disappearance on April 27.

News of Rachel’s disappearance was then made public on Tuesday in the UK with her family and friends jetting out to North Africa to help look for the Brit.



The UK Foreign Office also confirmed it was helping to support the family.

After a brief hunt, Rachel was then found in the same city but at an unknown apartment block.

Police found her using the country’s national security database.

She left her hotel of her own accord and hadn’t been subjected to any attack or threat to her physical safety, cops confirmed at around 5pm on Wednesday.

Peter Kerr, believed to be the Scot’s husband, quickly jumped on social media to claim Rachel hadn’t been found at 5:30pm.



At around 8pm he then posted: “Rachel has now been found and is with her brother.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A source close to the investigation later told The Sun that Rachel likely “wants to continue her vacation”.

Rachel is yet to make any comment on her disappearance of if she plans to remain in Morocco.

News.title: Two Green Party candidates arrested on suspicion of stirring up racial hatred for ‘posting antisemitic comments online’
News.content:
TWO Green Party candidates have been arrested on suspicion of stirring up racial hatred for allegedly posting antisemitic comments online.

One candidate allegedly claimed synagogue attacks were “revenge, not antisemitism”.





It is understood they posted a photo of a man holding a sign that read: “ramming a synagogue isn’t antisemitism, it’s revenge”.

Another reportedly posted a picture of an armed man in a Hamas headband with the slogan “Resistance is Freedom”.

According to The Telegraph, both were were detained by the Met Police on Thursday morning – just hours after an antisemitic terror attack in Golders Green, North London.

Following the double stabbing, Jewish leaders tore into politicians and police for the spike in antisemitic attacks.

Both the Met boss and a Labour minister were heckled by chants of “shame on you” as they visited the site of the terror attack yesterday.

Here’s everything you need to know about the Golders Green attack…



Cops scrambled to North London at 11.16am after reports that two people had been knifed in a brazen daylight attack.

The Met Police said the suspect tried to stab police officers before he was Tasered and arrested, but no cops were hurt.

Two stab victims, Shloime Rand and Moshe Shine, aged 76 and 34, were treated at the scene for stab wounds before being rushed to hospital.



A 45-year-old man, described by police as a British national born in Somalia, was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.

He was taken to hospital before later being discharged into police custody at a London police station.

The attack in Golders Green was formally declared a terrorist incident – and marks the sixth antisemitic attack in recent weeks.

Cops also believe the suspect was involved in another knife attack earlier in the day, in south east London.

It emerged today that he was referred to anti-terror programme Prevent in 2020 – but the case was closed.



A Green Party Spokesperson said: “This is now a police matter and we are unable to comment at this stage.”

Yesterday, Sir Mark Rowley said the individual in custody has a “history of serious violence and mental health issues”.

After he was Tasered and detained, he was taken to hospital but was later discharged and taken to a London police station.

Speaking after the terror rampage, the Met Commissioner was heckled by Jewish Londoners chanting “shame on you!”.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who is Jewish, has also been slammed for appearing to criticise the police who detained the alleged attacker.



The left-winger retweeted a post condemning the cops for kicking the suspect in the head when he refused to drop his weapon.

Scotland Yard has praised its “brave” officers for tackling the suspect and released footage of them taking him down using a Taser.

But Mr Polanski reposted an X comment that said: “So essentially his officers were repeatedly and violently kicking a mentally ill man in the head when he was already incapacitated by a Taser.”



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has vowed to “strain every sinew” to end the stain of antisemitism.

Following Wednesday’s attack in Golders Green, the government has announced an extra £25m in funding for increased police patrols and security in Jewish communities.

It says the funding will also be used to put further protections in place around synagogues, schools and community centres.

The announcement came after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for Starmer to do more to protect Jewish communities.

His statement slammed “weakness” in the face of “one antisemitic attack after another”.



It continued: “Words are not enough to confront this scourge.

“We demand and expect action by the British government to protect the Jews of England and bring antisemites to justice.”

The PM was met with chants calling him a “traitor” in the wake of the antisemitic terror attack in the North London suburb.

He convened a Cobra meeting after cops confirmed the attack had officially been declared a terror incident.

Today, chants against Sir Keir could be heard as he arrived at Hatzola Northwest Ambulance depot.



Placards showed Starmer’s face on a mask being held by former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn with the words “Keir Starmer Jew Harmer”.

News.title: PM is booed & met with chants of ‘Keir Starmer, Jew harmer!’ as local community reels after antisemitic attack
News.content:
SIR Keir Starmer has been met by mobs of angry protesters chanting “Keir Starmer, Jew Harmer” in Golders Green.

The Prime Minister was met with chants calling him a “traitor” in the wake of the antisemitic terror attack in the North London suburb.





Speaking yesterday, the PM slammed the double stabbing – which marks the sixth antisemitic incident in just a few weeks – as “appalling”.

He convened a Cobra meeting after cops confirmed the attack had officially been declared a terror incident.



And today, chants against Sir Keir could be heard as he arrived at Hatzola Northwest Ambulance depot on Finchley Road.

Placards showed Starmer’s face on a mask being held by former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn with the words “Keir Starmer Jew Harmer”.



Police had to hold back dozens of angry protesters as the PM arrived alongside his Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood.

Here’s everything you need to know about the Golders Green attack…

Sir Keir was spotted meeting with members of Shomrim – the Jewish community security organisation – who helped detain the suspect.



Shocking footage showed the moment the heroic locals held down the alleged knifeman as cops tried to remove his blade.

Niaz Maleknia, 57, was one of the demonstrators protesting as Sir Keir Starmer visited the ambulance service.

She said: “I can’t stand this man, so that’s why I’m here, because he has done nothing but stand in the way of Donald Trump and Israel.

“The reason why this place is such a mess and we’re all getting attacked is because of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and he’s standing with them.

“So that’s why I’m here, because this man just needs waking up.”



Niaz, who is Iranian-Jewish, said she wants the Government to proscribe the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation.

The PM and Ms Mahmood spent an hour and 20 minutes meeting with ambulance service volunteers and members of Shromrim.

Sir Keir was again heckled by protesters who demanded “show your face” and “protect our children” as he was driven off this afternoon.

Following the double-stabbing, Jewish leaders tore into politicians and police for the spike in antisemitic attacks.

Both the Met boss and a Labour minister were heckled by chants of “shame on you” as they visited the site of the terror attack.



PM 'not willing to take basic steps to protect British Jews' Exclusive By Julia Atherley SIR Keir Starmer is “not willing to take the basic steps that will protect British Jews”, the leader of the Campaign Against Antisemitism has blasted. Gideon Falter, chief executive of CAA, has renewed calls for the PM to immediately ban the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps – who he says are clearly behind the recent rise in attacks. He told The Sun: “I think it’s pretty clear that anti-Semitism in London is out of control. “We’ve got a situation now where British children are being radicalised. Iran’s orchestrating terrorism on our streets. “Our cities are overrun with these hate marches, and our politicians and police are busy appeasing extremists. “It’s a national emergency, but we’ve yet to see any evidence that the Prime Minister has a plan. “The reaction within the Jewish community has turned from fear to fury because we all see that we are being completely abandoned at the time when we are in desperately need of help. “The British Jewish community is an extremely patriotic, integrated community, which gives its all to this country. “The only expectation that British Jews have ever had is that we would just be left to get on with our lives just like everybody else. “Hate has come to our door, and we’ve now seen synagogues being set alight, ambulances being burnt to the ground because they belong to a Jewish charity, now yet more blood spilled in the streets this time in Golders Green. “There is yet to be the announcement of anything that anybody in the Jewish community seriously thinks is going to move the needle on this.” On what Sir Keir Starmer needs to do now, he said: “The absolute basics are obvious to him, and we’ve been saying them all along. “If he is unable to see that our schools and universities have become radicalisation grounds, if he’s unable to ban the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Muslim Brotherhood, which most countries in the Arab world have banned, then he’s unable to take basic steps. “He’s showing that he’s not willing to take the basic steps that will protect British Jews. “The hate marshes on our streets: We’ve been saying for a very long time that they are dangerous and full of extremists. Nothing has been done about them of any great note. “We need a prime minister who’s going to stand behind the lecture and not just tell us that he is deeply concerned with these pathetic political platitudes, but is actually going to tell us what specific, meaningful actions his government is going to take to stop this wave of terrorist attacks on Britain’s streets.” He called the funding announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood this morning as “practically inconsequential”, adding: “We cannot just keep building higher walls and employing more and more security guards. “Funding more security essentially says that Jews have to live behind 24/7 security guards, even ambulances need to be guarded now. “The reality is that we need to go after the problem that it’s at its source and Britain has no strategy and no approach for stopping the foreign interference in our country and stopping the radicalisation of British kids.” On the terror group claiming responsibility for the attack, he said: “We believe that this group is essentially a front for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. It’s the Iranian state that is acting under a different logo. “Everybody can see through it and the security services know that this is the case as well. “The only people pretending that we are not under attack by a foreign state seems to be our government, which says that we’re uninvolved with Iran and that is not appropriate to ban the Israel Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.” He called for “decent ordinary Brits” to stand up to radicals they encounter “whether in their friends, family, workplace, wherever”. He urged them to tell them “they are having no impact whatsoever on events thousands of miles away in the Middle East but what they are doing is creating the kind of incendiary situation in which these attacks happen and British blood is spilled on British streets”.

Speaking after the terror rampage, the Met Commissioner was heckled by Jewish Londoners chanting “shame on you!”.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has also been slammed for appearing to criticise the police who detained the alleged attacker.

The left-winger retweeted a post condemning the cops for kicking the suspect in the head when he refused to drop his weapon.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has vowed to “strain every sinew” to end the stain of anti-Semitism.

The North London suburb was plunged into lockdown yesterday after two men, aged 34 and 76, were stabbed in a terror attack.



Local police and armed officers rushed to the scene at 11.16am – after the rampage unfolded in just four minutes – before detaining the suspect.

The Sun understands the alleged attacker came to the UK legally as a child from Somalia in the 1990s.

And the suspect was known to Prevent – the government’s anti-terror and deradicalisation programme – the Met Police confirmed today.

The two victims – named as Shloime Rand and Moshe Shine – were treated at the scene for stab wounds before being rushed to hospital.

And cops last night revealed the suspect had been involved in another knife “altercation” just hours before the horror unfolded in Golders Green.



Officers were called to an incident in Southwark, South London – seven miles away from the scene of the terror attack – at around 8.50am.

Police said the suspect had a knife and was involved in a confrontation with the occupant, who suffered minor injuries.

Following yesterday’s attack, the government has announced an extra £25m in funding for increased police patrols in Jewish communities.

It says the funding will also be used to put further security and protections in place around synagogues, schools and community centres.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The announcement came after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for Starmer to do more to protect Jewish communities.



Israel blamed government policies “that embolden and legitimize Islamist elements” and accused ministers of “tolerating unchecked incitement”.

News.title: My son was a sweet teddy bear who turned into a demon, I drove him to the woods to shoot him, I only wish he had died
News.content:
MONSTER'S MOTHER My son was a sweet teddy bear who turned into a demon, I drove him to the woods to shoot him, I only wish he had died

WHEN he was a young child, Jeanette Halton-Tiggs adored her son, Timmy, who had chubby cheeks and liked to wear a suit and tie like the ministers in church.

“He wanted to be a minister and told me, ‘Mama, I have to look the part,’” says Jeanette.





It’s a memory that makes her smile – but that is soon eclipsed by the darkest of shadows, that saw her son grow up with a love for inflicting pain on his younger sister, escalating into violent outbursts on others and the shooting of a police officer.

Terrified for the safety of her family, Jeanette made the unthinkable decision to kill her own son. She drove to the park to shoot him and aimed her gun at him but couldn’t go through with it at the last moment.

“Timmy was my big sweet teddy bear that morphed into a monster,” she says. “I love my son dearly, but if I would have killed him, police officer Jason West would still be alive.”

In the TV documentary, Evil Lives Here: My Child The Killer, Jeanette talks about her fears and the trauma of watching her cherubic son turn into a demon.

“As a parent, you always blame yourself. You always question, ‘Did I do enough? What could I have done different? I mean, he was just so adorable growing up, with those cheeks that everybody would squeeze. I have a lot of happy memories. I just have a lot of sad ones, too.”



A year after Timmy was born, Jeanette gave birth to her daughter, Chrissy. The following year, she filed for divorce.

“Married at 16, two kids by 17, divorced at 18. I didn’t know how to do this thing. I didn’t know how to raise children. They were being raised along with me.”



Her grandmother helped watch the children while Jeanette worked two jobs in her home town of Cleveland, Ohio.

“It was hard. My son would be on the sidewalk, looking down the street at his father, who didn’t visit him, teaching another kid how to ride a bike.

“He was influenced by seeing his grandfather preaching from the church pulpit and his father playing the organ and wanted to go to bible school to study to become a minister.

“He wanted to ‘look the part’ from an early age so we would go to the department store and while I’m looking for T-shirts, sweatshirts and pants, he’d be off in the little suit department and I couldn’t say no to him. He’d be so happy. He was like a little man. He thought he was man of the house and was my protector.

“He was so loving and he and his sister were so close. They were best friends. But then he changed.



“One day I smelt something really foul and I’m looking around and finally, I checked under Timmy’s bed and opened a shoe box to find a dead bird inside that had been cut open. It freaked me out.

“I called him in and I asked him about it and he didn’t answer at first but then he said, ‘I was just putting it out of its misery.’

“I did not want to think that my son could be cruel. I was frightened. I just knew something was wrong with him because I had heard that psychopaths start off by killing animals and I thought, maybe he is a demon.

“I made every excuse up you can. That’s what mothers do. We love our babies so much and we want the best for them. We don’t want to think the worst, but I didn’t know what was coming next.”

One night, while she was getting Chrissy ready for her bath, Jeanette noticed marks on her daughter’s leg.



“I asked her what caused them and she tried to cover them up but then said, ‘Timmy made this shocking toy and he shocks me. He burns me and he told me that if I told you he was going to get me.’

PICS

“He would tie her to a chair and, I don’t know quite how he did it, but he would take wires out of a radio and he would shock her with them. Everything became very real in that moment. He was physically abusing his little sister.

“I didn’t want to spank my children, but there was no stopping me. But even when I did that, he showed no emotion.”

Timmy promised never to hurt his sister again. But it was a promise he wouldn’t keep.



“A couple of weeks later, I came home early from work and Chrissy’s in a chair. I said, ‘Is he shocking you again?’ And she said, ‘Yeah, mummy.’

“She told me the louder she yelled or screeched, the more he laughed about it. I tried to talk to him in an attempt to get to the bottom of why he liked to inflict pain but he would just say, ‘I don’t know why.’

“The family said that we should pray the demon inside him, away. They literally wanted to do an exorcism in the church. I know there’s a God and I believe there’s hell, too. There was something evil inside of him.”

After a series of violent incidents when he was a teenager, Timmy was sent to a school for children with behavioural issues. Here, he had to be restrained in a straitjacket after attacking a teacher for asking about his father.

Despite the violence, Timmy was academically smart and was proud to be able to tell his mum he had won a place at college.



“I was so proud of him and he was so happy that I was proud of him because he had caused me so much heartache and pain. It gave me so much hope. I thought he was getting it together and that we had turned a corner.”

Unfortunately, Timmy couldn’t stop the violence inside of him. He assaulted multiple people in various incidents. “He would hang out at the mall and punch people in the head for no reason,” she said.

On 9 July, 2000, when he was 20, police got a call from Chrissy who had locked her brother out of the house. She described him as bipolar and “Violent when not properly medicated.” A disorderly conduct charge was later dismissed.

“That was part of the problem,” says Jeanette. “No matter what he did, no matter who he hurt, they dismissed him. He just got one slap on the wrist after another.”

Because of his behavioural issues, his school determined he was not ready for college. Hoping to help her son, Jeanette sent him to a psychiatric facility for evaluation. While here, he had to be put into a straitjacket again after attacking the nurses.



“I went to see him and I will never forget his face. It was not my son, I swear to God. It’s so hard to make anyone believe, but I was looking at a devil.”

After Timmy was released from the facility, his violent behaviour continued to spiral out of control.

“He would walk around the house screaming and punching holes in the walls. Chrissy was terrified of him. She had a new baby and she was scared to sleep alone so she and the baby would sleep with me. She said that if we kicked him out, he would get us. The situation was so hopeless. I bought a gun for our protection.”

One night, Chrissy called her mum in a state of terror. Timmy was on a rampage.

“I rushed home and when I got there, I saw blood on the wall and I got my gun out of my purse and looked around. I didn’t know if he was still in the house.”



Jeanette found Chrissy and her baby hiding in the closet. She had already rung the police and when they arrived, they searched the house but Timmy was not there. However, outside, they found the cat, cut up, which is where the blood came from.

In 2003, Timmy was arrested for attacking a police officer. He was put on probation for four years and had to stay medicated and monitored. It seemed to work.

“It was a miracle. I noticed a big difference. He worked six days a week. He was so proud of himself. He bought a brand new car, he finally moved out of my house and had a girlfriend. But after a year they took him off probation because he was doing so well. I said to the probation officer, ‘But what about his medication?’ and she said, ‘Oh, that ends too.’

“I was like, ‘Are you serious? Look over his records. Please reconsider. You’re going to keep letting my son go until he kills somebody.’”

Feeling like she was not getting any help from elsewhere, Jeanette decided to take matters into her own hands.



She persuaded Timmy to go to the park with her, where they sometimes used to sit on a bench. But this time she had an ulterior motive. She had packed her gun and intended to shoot him.

“I said to him, ‘Timmy, look over there,’ and he got up to look at where I was pointing and I took out my gun and pointed it at him to shoot him in the back of the head. But my hands were trembling and I just dropped it, fell to my knees, and I let out this horrible scream.

“He ran back, saying, ‘Mummy, what’s wrong?’ He didn’t understand why I was crying and I never told him.”

On 25 May, 2007, Timmy, now 27, made her worst nightmare become a reality when he shot police officer Jason West as he attended a fight in the street. In court, Timmy raged that the officer pulled a gun on him and denied shooting him but then admitted that he shot Jason, who had not drawn his gun, four times.

On 30 October, 2009, he was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.



“After the incident, I was fearful of retaliation for my whole family,” says Jeanette. “I would be so ashamed. I would walk with my head down, hoping they didn’t recognise me. He’s the monster and I’m the monster’s mother. It’s an awful feeling.

“There’s a memorial sign to Jason West that I drive past twice a day, to work and back. I say a quick prayer for him and his family each time.

“Timmy just turned 46 but he’s still my baby. You never stop loving them. But, as awful as it sounds, I wish Timmy had died that night instead of Jason.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“That would have been a better outcome for everybody. And if I had killed him then Jason West would still be alive. I’m not proud to say that, but it’s the truth. “

Evil Lives Here: My Child The Killer, Quest Red, Thursday 30 April, 9pm

News.title: Man and woman in their 20s found dead in Premier Inn hotel room as cops probe ‘unexplained’ death
News.content:
HOTEL TRAGEDY Man and woman in their 20s found dead in Premier Inn hotel room as cops probe ‘unexplained’ death

AN INVESTIGATION has been launched after a man and a woman in their 20s were tragically found dead in a Premier Inn.

Cops launched a probe after the bodies of the pair were found in one of the rooms at the hotel in Ipswich, Suffolk, on Tuesday afternoon.





Emergency crews were scrambled to the premises – which has 85 rooms across six floors – at around 2.30pm.

Five police cars, two police vans and an ambulance could be seen outside the three star hotel.

Suffolk Police confirmed the deaths are being treated as unexplained, but believe there are no suspicious circumstances.

The force said: “Police were called to an address in Key Street, Ipswich by the ambulance service shortly before 2.30pm on Tuesday.

“A man and woman were found dead within the address and their families have been notified.

“Enquiries are at an early stage and at present the deaths are being treated as unexplained, however they are currently not believed to be suspicious.”

It is believed that police are preparing a file on the deaths for the coroner and are awaiting the results of a post mortem.

The Sun has approached Premier Inn for comment.

News.title: Mother-in-law of ‘murdered’ beauty queen, 27, arrested after going on the run as husband ‘breastfed baby from her body’
News.content:
THE mother-in-law of murdered Mexican beauty queen Carolina Flores Gomez has been arrested after going on the run.

It comes after reports the tragic model’s husband tried to breastfeed their baby with her dead body before alerting police.





Erika Maria Herrera, 63, also known as “N” was cuffed following a major police manhunt – after 27-year-old Carolina was shot dead on April 15.

The mum-in-law and main suspect in the case was arrested in Venezuela following an urgent search.

The shooting took place at a luxury apartment in Mexico City – with horror footage showing the moments before Carolina’s death.

Carolina’s husband Alejandro said he tried to breastfeed their baby using her corpse and only alerted authorities the day after her death.



The beauty queen’s mum has accused Alejandro of deliberately delaying his call to police in order to give his own mother time to escape.

Investigators have not confirmed the claims.



Mexico police said: “The Attorney General’s Office of Mexico City confirms that, in coordination with authorities of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, Erika Maria ‘N’ was arrested as the probable person responsible for the femicide of a 27-year-old woman committed in the Miguel Hidalgo borough.

“Following the murder, the City of Mexico Prosecutor’s Office initiated an investigation that made it possible to establish her probable involvement.

“Based on the evidence gathered on April 17, one day after the complaint was filed, a judge issued the corresponding arrest warrant.”



Mexican cops were helped by Interpol and the suspect is currently being held in Venezuela pending extradition.

Carolina, a former Miss Teen Universe, was shot dead in the face, neck and head.

Her husband Alejandro has claimed he decided to stay at home and not immediately report the shooting because he wanted to feed their baby, according to local crime reporter Carlos Jimenez.



He said he tried to breastfeed the tot – as Carolina had been doing at the time – and then bathed it before calling his lawyers.

Alejandro also claimed he feared the baby could be taken into care by social services.

Chilling footage from the day of Carolina’s death shows two women walking into a room before gunshots and screaming are heard.

Herrera was inside the home with her son – Carolina’s partner – at the time of the shooting in Polanco, Mexico City.

Alejandro has not been arrested but is understood to be under investigation for failing to report his wife’s death immediately.



In the harrowing video of Carolina’s death, the former pageant winner from Baja California can be seen walking to the back of her home wearing a white robe.

Several local outlets have reported Carolina was going to get her mother-in-law a drink of water at the time.

Herrera is then seen following her before several gunshots ring out.

The victim’s husband, Alejandro, walks into the frame just seconds later, carrying the couple’s baby.

“What was that?” he asks his mother in Spanish.



“What did you do, crazy?” an unidentified person’s voice is heard saying.

“Nothing,” his mum answers. “She made me angry.”

“What’s wrong with you? She’s my family,” Alejandro says, calmly.

His mum replies: “You’re mine and she stole you”.

Spanish media outlet Debate spoke to a close friend of Carolina, who said the victim had been hounded by her mother-in-law when she fell pregnant.



The friend said Carolina believed that Herrera “never liked her” and that she had “gotten worse” since the pregnancy.

It has also been suggested that a multimillion-pound inheritance could be behind the killing.

Carolina is believed to have received a large sum of money following the death of her father.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The high-profile killing left the Mexican community reeling, sparking a wave of protests in Mexico‘s Baja California over the weekend.

Carolina was born in San Diego, was crowned Miss Teen Universe for Baja California in 2017, and picked up several local titles in her home city of Ensenada.

News.title: Brits urged to 'take action' on 'tedious' admin tasks - or they could risk being cut off
News.content:
Brits urged to 'take action' on 'tedious' admin tasks - or they could risk being cut off

Brits who commonly put off booking important appointments or paying bills could see themselves facing late fees or having services cut off

View 3 Images Avoiding certain admin tasks can lead to late fees or losing access to services (Image: PinPep)

Brits delay crucial life admin for over three months before eventually getting round to tackling it. Research involving 2,000 adults found booking MOTs, settling credit card bills, completing tax returns and arranging doctor's appointments are amongst the most frequently postponed tasks.

‌



Nearly half confessed these administrative duties take a back seat because they give priority to other responsibilities, while others say they have a lack of time, or it's not a pressing enough matter. Yet 30% have put off something important for such a long time that they ended up missing a deadline, leading to late fees or losing access to crucial services.

‌



View 3 Images BT wants to highlight the importance of tackling admin tasks straight away (Image: PinPep)

‌



A quarter have missed settling an electricity or water bill, while 21% have neglected to renew a direct debit. Consequently, 13% lost access to vital services like water and electricity, and one in 10 (9%) were prevented from driving their vehicles.

The research was commissioned by BT's Digital Voice service to highlight awareness of the transition from analogue landlines to digital, which could result in a customer's service being interrupted if they don't respond when contacted about it.

It turns out, 29% have ignored or delayed responding to messages from a provider about an essential service like the digital landline switch, and only 18% said they immediately take action when they are reminded of tasks.

‌



Behavioural psychologist Jo Hemmings, which has teamed up with the brand, said: "Often, people procrastinate over life admin because the tasks feel overwhelming or tedious, and our brains are wired to seek out activities that are more immediately rewarding.

"There's also a sense of avoidance at play, we tend to underestimate the consequences of delay and overestimate the effort required to get started. Ultimately, we can all be guilty of putting things off, but when there's a deadline looming, as in the case of the nationwide switchover to digital landlines, it's time to take action."

‌



Clare Balding, who is working with the provider to encourage customers to act promptly when contacted, said: "When your provider gets in touch, it's vitally important you act to ensure your landline services keeps running smoothly. If you don't respond, the services you rely on could be disrupted."

View 3 Images Clare Balding meets BT customer, John Garrard, age 77, to discuss the digital landline switch (Image: PinPep)

More than three quarters (77%) wished they possessed more of a 'take action' mindset to prevent missing crucial deadline dates for life admin. But 50% disclosed they handle the majority of admin in their household, compared to 20% who divide it equally with their partner.

‌



Meanwhile 21% also oversee the life admin for people beyond the household, on top of the average of five tasks most people tackle each and every month. Of those who assist others completing their household management, 72% said this affects their capacity to manage their own life admin.

Yet 75% of those polled, via OnePoll, felt confident about handling important life admin tasks which involve changing technology, like making the transition to digital landlines.

BT Digital Voice spokesperson, Lucy Baker, said: "As our research shows, it's easy to overlook messages from service providers, but doing so could disrupt essential connections when it comes to the digital landline switch.

Article continues below

"It's important to take action when contacted, so everyone can benefit from more reliable, secure technology and stay connected to the services they rely on."

News.title: 'I got cancer diagnosis and my husband's reaction has been so hurtful'
News.content:
'I got cancer diagnosis and my husband's reaction has been so hurtful'

Dealing with a cancer diagnosis can be frightening and anxiety-inducing. One woman thought she'd be able to count on her husband for his support during her diagnosis, but his reaction has floored her

View Image The woman has been floored by her husband's reaction to her cancer diagnosis (stock image) (Image: witthaya_prasongsin/Getty Images)

A woman currently dealing with a diagnosis of cervical cancer has been left stunned by her husband’s reaction to her situation. According to Cancer Research, 3,299 new cases of cervical cancer are identified every year. The charity added 880 people in the UK died from the disease from 2022 until 2024, but “99.8 per cent of cervical cancer cases are preventable”.

‌



Dealing with any kind of cancer diagnosis is a challenging, anxiety-inducing and daunting time. Typically, married people expect to be able to rely on their spouse, especially given the famed “in sickness and in health” portion of traditional wedding vows.

‌



But one woman has explained how she's felt her husband has been “emotionally absent the entire time”. She said he “won’t engage in conversations”, has avoided “being there for important moments”, and even “ignored” her after she had surgery.

‌



Taking to Reddit, she said: “I feel completely alone and don’t know how to handle a partner who seems indifferent during something this serious.” The 28-year-old woman explained her ordeal in full detail, looking for advice from fellow Reddit users.

She said that “from the start”, she’s been to “every single appointment” by herself, including her biopsy, and when she tries to talk to her husband about how “scared” she is, “he just gives short, dismissive responses” and “shuts the conversation down.”

She described how she had wanted to stay at home with her husband when she was due to receive her medical imaging results as she was feeling “anxious and terrified” about what the results might reveal. But he refused because he wanted to attend a DJ event at a bar with his friends.

‌



He insisted he had “made a commitment” to them and, after the couple “went back and forth”, she ended up going with him because she “didn’t want to find out the results alone”.

While at the event, she discovered her husband’s friend’s wife was pregnant. Although she tried her “best to be happy and supportive”, she said she felt “devastated" knowing she wouldn't be able to have more children - and was even more hurt after learning her husband had known his friend’s wife was pregnant beforehand.

The woman then discovered she has a 2cm tumour on her cervix and “ended up just crying alone upstairs”. When she tried to talk to her husband about it, he “brushed her off” because “he was busy with his friends”.

‌



After having a procedure to remove cells from her cervix and obtain a biopsy of the tumour under general anaesthesia, her husband was meant to be there to support her - but said “he had a toothache”. She said: “I spent my time in post-op helping him find a dentist and manage his pain.

"He complained that it was taking so long (short 30 min procedure and one hour in post-op). At discharge, the nurse tried to explain my instructions to him because I was still out of it and in pain. He was scrolling on Instagram and not paying attention. I had to call his name multiple times just to get him to sign the paperwork.”

Article continues below

Once they got home, she did “all the nightly chores, let the dogs out, and struggled to follow her post-op care” while her husband “sat on the couch watching YouTube”. The woman found everything “physically difficult and exhausting” after her procedure.

When her husband visited the pharmacy, he “only picked up medication for his toothache” and “not the prescriptions” ordered by the oncologist for his wife. She added: “I feel like I’m going through one of the scariest moments of my life completely alone, while also being treated like such a burden.”

Fellow Reddit users in the comments section were appalled and urged her to put herself first and leave her husband.

News.title: Sustainable home upgrades rise as UK homeowners cut luxuries for eco improvements
News.content:
Sustainable home upgrades rise as UK homeowners cut luxuries for eco improvements

UK homeowners are spending more on home improvements than ever before - sacrificing holidays and new cars to fund eco-friendly home improvements

View 2 Images Homeowners are 'future-proofing' their properties with energy efficient additions (Image: Daikin)

Homeowners are splashing out more cash on their properties than ever before – sacrificing other luxuries such as dining out and new cars in the process.

‌



A survey of 2,000 homeowners revealed that, despite widespread economic concerns, average spending has risen to £3,140 per year on home improvements – up from £2,870 in 2024.

‌



Nearly a third (30%) are planning to spend even more on home improvements in 2026 than they did last year, with homeowners cutting back on holiday plans (24%) and new car purchases (14%) in favour of renovations.

‌



Two thirds (67%) are redirecting their focus – and their finances – towards home improvement to prioritise comfort, while 32% want greater control over their energy bills, with 22% concerned about energy security, and 32% regularly worried about the price volatility of gas and electricity.

The survey, commissioned by heat pump manufacturer Daikin, also revealed that 63% consider investing in energy efficiency to be very important to them and 'future-proofing' their home against price fluctuations.

It found, 55% of homeowners believe making their property more energy efficient would boost its resale value, with 43% making these changes to attract future buyers, despite having no immediate plans to move.

‌



View 2 Images Investing in energy efficient improvements is important to two-thirds of homeowners (Image: Getty Images)

Nearly half (47%) said alternative energy sources like heat pumps and solar panels would be sound investments for their future.

Lucy Gaby, residential marketing manager from the heat pump brand said: "Most people spend the majority of their time at home, so it is imperative to make it a comfortable and relaxing space throughout the seasons, to cope with all conditions - from heatwaves to cold snaps."

‌



"We're seeing a clear shift in priorities, with homeowners increasingly willing to invest in their living environment rather than more traditional luxuries."

Lucy also notes that the Government's Boiler Upgrade Scheme, which offers grants up to £9,000, is making this more attainable. As does the Future Homes and Building Standards policy which establishes that new homes are expected to incorporate low-carbon heating and adhere to significantly higher energy efficiency standards.

"Creating an energy-efficient home not only boosts comfort but also helps manage rising energy costs and improve energy security," she adds.

‌



Enhancing insulation (35%), draught-proofing doors and windows (27%) and double or triple glazing (25%) are amongst the leading priorities for homeowners.

The research, conducted via OnePoll, revealed that when purchasing in the future, 46% would choose an energy efficient home over just 7% who would select a property requiring these improvements.

Nearly half (44%) even stated they would pay more for a low-energy consumption home.

Article continues below

Lucy Gaby from Daikin, featured at Grand Designs Live this weekend, added: "With fluctuations in weather conditions alongside energy price volatility, it's no surprise that future-proofing our homes is now top of mind for most of us. Investing in energy efficiency today is an investment in the comfort and security of tomorrow."

News.title: Phone users reveal biggest tech frustrations we can all relate to
News.content:
Phone users reveal biggest tech frustrations we can all relate to

The average tech user encounters tech-related frustrations twice a day – with phone anxiety, slow internet and digital stress among the most common triggers

View 2 Images Phone users are faced with tech frustrations on a daily basis (Image: Getty Images)

The top modern-day tech frustrations include tests to verify you're not a robot, being connected to the internet with no actual access – and dropping your phone on the floor. A survey of 2,000 Brits found sending messages to the wrong people, or making a bad typo in an important email, are enough to make many break out in a cold sweat.

‌



On average, tech users encounter tech‐related frustrations twice a day, rising to three among Gen Z and Millennials. Many added having just one bar of signal triggers instant stress, as does waking up to discover their phone hasn't charged properly overnight.

‌



View 2 Images Dropping your phone on the floor and seeing it smash is one of the top frustrations (Image: © SWNS)

‌



A spokesperson from Samsung, which commissioned the research to mark the launch of the Galaxy A57 5G, built with water and scratch resistance and Super Fast Charging 2.0, said: "Life moves fast, and your tech should keep up. It plays a huge role in helping people juggle busy lives, so it's important to have devices you can rely on."

Over a quarter of Boomers (27%) get their stress levels rising when they can't remember their password. But snap happy younger adults turn red when their phone's storage reaches capacity (22%). Others admitted they dread seeing their messages left 'on read'.

‌



In addition, 17% experience connectivity issues daily, such as no signal or painfully slow internet, despite 86% needing to be connected to the internet all the time.

This goes on to cause stress for 65%, with 85% adding they value the peace of mind that comes from knowing their device will last the day and work when they need it.

The findings point to a growing shift in what people value most in their devices, with reliability a defining factor.

Article continues below

Over eight in 10 (85%) said they value the peace of mind that comes from knowing their device will last the day and work when they need it.

The Samsung spokesperson added: "That's why so much effort goes into designing devices that work seamlessly in the background – so they support your day instead of interrupting it."

News.title: 'Sandwich generation' get just 8 days a year of 'me time' as mental health suffers
News.content:
'Sandwich generation' get just 8 days a year of 'me time' as mental health suffers

Those caring for both older and younger relatives get just eight days of personal time a year, with two-thirds saying the limited time to themselves has impacted their mental health.

Hussain Manawer shares his care experience with AXA Health

The 'sandwich generation' gets just eight days a year to themselves – three times less than those without any dependants enjoy. A poll of 2,000 adults discovered those juggling both older and younger relatives depending on them face the greatest pressure when it comes to spare time and self-care.

‌



Those who are part of the 'sandwich generation' manage just under four hours of personal time a week - equivalent to around eight days annually - yet dedicate 11-and-a-half hours weekly doing things for others. By contrast, the typical adult without any caring duties will have an average of 12-and-a-half hours of leisure time each week.

‌



View 2 Images Hussain Manawer (pictured) understands the experience of 'carrying burden of care' (Image: PinPep)

‌



Nearly half (48%) of the 'sandwich generation' acknowledged they have less time to themselves than they'd prefer, with 67% believing this has affected their mental health and 66% feeling the same about their physical wellbeing.

The research, commissioned by AXA Health as part of its Cover That Cares campaign, also revealed 44% of the 'sandwich generation' consistently put others before themselves. Yet 36% believe as a group they are frequently overlooked by society.

The health insurer partnered with best-selling author, poet and mental health campaigner Hussain Manawer to compose a poem capturing the realities of caring for ourselves and others.

‌



Hussain said: "It was exciting to work on this poem and bring to life how the sandwich generation feel, while giving care a voice.

"I've first hand experience of carrying the burden of care, which made working on this poem deeply important to me and I hope helps share a message for anyone who feels that way."

View 2 Images Hussain's poem is part of AXA's Cover That Cares campaign (Image: PinPep)

‌



The research revealed that 14% of those in the sandwich generation can't recall the last time they did something purely for themselves. A quarter of them even regard food shopping and household chores as 'me time' simply because it involves time spent alone.

The knock-on effect of having less 'me time' than they would like has left 51% of the 'sandwich generation' feeling stressed, 45% unable to switch off and 37% without any time to pursue their own hobbies.

The mental burden of coordinating their lives is highlighted as an obstacle to securing more personal time by 27%. Likewise, 16% confessed they experience guilt about having 'me time'.

‌



In a perfect scenario, they revealed their solo time would involve unwinding, reading and working out. Additional free time would ideally be devoted to their partner, on family rambles or heading to the pictures with relatives.

To carve out any time for themselves, the OnePoll research discovered those in the sandwich generation must schedule it well ahead (26%), compared to merely 11% of those without caring duties.

Crucial support for this demographic was identified as having someone to 'share the load' with, simply having a sympathetic ear and a physical gesture such as an embrace.

‌



Others revealed that having people surrounding them who grasp what they're experiencing helps, as does a reassuring text message or phone call.

Heather Smith, CEO of AXA Health, said: "This group juggles caring for multiple generations and leaves little time for themselves, which as the stats show, has impacted both their physical and mental health.

"Hussain's poem represents this and brings to life how those in the sandwich generation are struggling and how something as small as an understanding text message can make a difference.

‌



"Sometimes all people need is to be seen and heard and we hope our members know we're here to listen and support them when they need us."

YOU MAKE ME FEEL SEEN - POEM BY HUSSAIN MANAWER

You show up for me without me asking

Notice the shift in my mood,

‌



the way my body reacts to the never ending list of things to do

The way my shoulders carry unfinished tasks

the way my eyes are glancing

‌



You show up for me with an oat latte,

A hug you know I need

A shoulder to rest my overthinking head,

‌



Without me asking

As time grows on and life moves on

‌



I’m learning to be, still, for a moment

To relax and not be too hard on myself

To breathe, that it’s ok with everything going to also

‌



Prioritise me

See I do listen,

exactly how you taught me

‌



Before you ask, I’ve done the bed sheets

The dishes too, The clothes are hung up to dry

‌



The dust by the windows is gone, for now too,

You don’t need to say it,

But it works the same way back,

‌



I appreciate everything you do for me too

Thank you, you're probably thinking for what?

‌



Well, I’m thanking you, because I feel your care,

through your warmth and love

Your messages that arrive at the right time that re-assure me

‌



I’m good, everything’s ok, and that I’m not too much

I understand, we may not always have the chance to be there for each other

‌



We’re busy and that’s nobody’s fault,

I get it, time just really flies for you and me,

so, with or without you in the room

Article continues below

Or wherever you are, I just want you to know, I'm grateful for your support

And you do, you make me feel seen.

News.title: Queen Camilla has one particular drink at lunch as she says 'there's no point otherwise’
News.content:
Queen Camilla has one particular drink at lunch as she says 'there's no point otherwise’

Queen Camilla loves full-fat Coca-Cola and wine while King Charles prefers martinis - discover the Royal Family's surprising drink preferences and dining habits

View 4 Images Queen Camilla likes to drink a specific beverage at lunch (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Even the most dedicated royals find time to unwind, and many members of the Royal Family have made no secret of their love for a quiet tipple. The late Queen Mother was famously partial to a cocktail of her own creation — Gin and Dubonnet, served with a slice of lemon and lashings of ice.

‌



Her fondness for this potent concoction certainly didn't do her any harm. The Queen Mother lived to the remarkable age of 101, and her daughter, the late Queen Elizabeth II, inherited not only her mother's longevity but also her preference for a 70% Dubonnet and 30% gin blend.

‌



The late Queen's sister, Princess Margaret, had rather "simple tastes" when it came to her drinking habits, according to the Queen Mother's private secretary Sir Martin Gilliat. Princess Margaret's tipple of choice was Famous Grouse whisky, served simply over ice, and she was never shy about making her displeasure known if the ice cubes had been left to melt.

‌



Today's royals, however, appear to be a considerably more restrained bunch. The Daily Mail's Rebecca English, who has been travelling alongside King Charles and Queen Camilla on their tour of the USA this week, disclosed that the Queen "loves a glass of Coke, but only ever full fat, never diet because there's 'no point otherwise'."

View 4 Images While she has a strong association with the wine trade, Camilla often goes for a Coke (Image: Getty)

Notably, the Queen also serves as president of the UK Vineyards Association and has previously made clear her appreciation for a glass of fine wine.

‌



Speaking at a reception for the Worshipful Company of Vintners earlier this year, Camilla said that her love of wine had been instilled in her during childhood: "Probably everybody knows my love of wine, it's in my blood and I was brought up by a father whose passion was wine, without a doubt," she said.

The Queen, whose late father was wine merchant Major Bruce Shand, added: "We drank wine as children, we grew up like the French", and recalled learning "how to spit properly".

View 4 Images The King and Queen will also sample the occasional pint (Image: Pool/Tim Graham Royal Photos, Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)

‌



Her son, Tom Parker-Bowles, told You Magazine in an interview that Camilla's desert island meal would probably be washed down with "a really good glass of red claret"

In contrast, His Majesty The King has a fondness for a martini, according to Palace Papers author Tina Brown, and savours the 50/50 blend of gin and dry vermouth at least once daily.

The Telegraph's royal correspondent Gordon Rayner reveals that the King is so exacting about his favourite tipple being served "just so" that he even travels with his own spirits and his own glass, to guarantee the cocktail is prepared perfectly.

‌



View 4 Images The Queen has tried an occasional pint (Image: Getty)

His Majesty is also known to appreciate a dram of fine Scotch from time to time, and has bestowed upon Laphroaig's 15 year old single malt a prized royal warrant.

Never one to overlook a commercial opportunity, King Charles also markets his own Highgrove Organic Single Malt Scotch for a not insignificant £36 per bottle.

Article continues below

Those who aren't particularly keen on whisky will be glad to know that the King's Highgrove estate also crafts its own organic gin, priced at £39.95 a bottle, alongside a rather appealing honey-infused rum that will set you back £44.95.

News.title: Fears over future of Motability as drivers already avoid it before July change
News.content:
Fears over future of Motability as drivers already avoid it before July change

Drivers say 'significant upfront costs and limited choice' are already major barriers

View 3 Images Disabled drivers rely on the scheme to support their transport costs

Disabled drivers across the UK already struggling with the cost of motoring have been told changes to the Motability Scheme risk making the lifeline even harder to access. A Carwow investigation found that 92% of people with disabilities rely on driving but more than two thirds already avoid the Motability Scheme due to cost.

‌



Siobhan Doyle, Consumer Writer at Carwow said: “Motability is often viewed as a 'free car' scheme, with a wide choice of vehicles, but the reality is very different. Only 59% of the disabled drivers we surveyed were eligible for the scheme in the first place, and of those, just a third have a car through the scheme, which is just 19% overall, with most citing significant upfront costs and limited choice as major barriers.”

‌



Carwow data shows that for more than a third of disabled drivers, finding a car that meets their needs is the biggest challenge, while 28% say unaffordable vehicle adaptations are a key barrier.

‌



View 3 Images Around 890,000 Britons use the Motability scheme (Alamy/PA)

From July 1, 2026, changes to the Motability Scheme - including reduced mileage allowances (30,000 miles over three years), higher excess mileage charges (25p per mile), and tighter cost limits - will apply to new customers. While intended to support the scheme’s long-term sustainability, there are growing concerns that they will add further strain for drivers already struggling to access suitable vehicles.

‌



Siobhan said: “Our data shows that driving isn’t a luxury for disabled people - it’s essential. But many are already being squeezed by rising costs, limited choice and poor accessibility. There’s also a persistent misunderstanding around the scheme. The perception that disabled people are handed ‘free cars’ simply isn’t accurate, and it masks the real financial and practical challenges many face.

View 3 Images Drivers say the scheme is already difficult

“With changes to Motability on the horizon, there’s a real risk these issues will deepen, leaving some drivers with fewer options and reduced independence. More broadly, this points to a widening gap between what disabled drivers need and what the current system delivers, particularly as costs increase and the shift to electric vehicles creates new accessibility hurdles.

Article continues below

“Without greater focus from policymakers and manufacturers on affordability, vehicle design and infrastructure, there’s a danger that access to mobility - and the independence it enables - will become even more limited.”

News.title: NHS GP Dr Amir Khan shares 5 natural ways to lower your blood pressure
News.content:
NHS GP Dr Amir Khan shares 5 natural ways to lower your blood pressure

Around 14.4 million people in the UK have high blood pressure, and NHS GP Dr Amir Khan has shared five natural ways to help lower your blood pressure to reduce risk of heart attacks and stroke

View Image Dr Amir Khan shared five ways you can reduce your blood pressure naturally (Image: ITV)

Dr Amir Khan has revealed five measures you can take to naturally reduce your blood pressure. According to the British Heart Foundation, approximately 14.4 million people across the UK are affected by high blood pressure, the equivalent of one in three adults. However, only about nine million have received an official diagnosis from their GP.

‌



To assist people in preventing the condition, or simply aid those looking to lower their high blood pressure, NHS GP Dr Amir Khan, a frequently face on ITV's Lorraine and GMB, has outlined five lifestyle changes you can adopt to maintain healthy blood pressure levels. "Let's talk about five natural ways to lower your blood pressure," he said at the start of his social media video.

‌



"Now, blood pressure is the force of your blood against the walls of your arteries." He went on to explain: "There are two numbers [when testing your blood pressure]. The top one is the force of the blood as your heart squeezes to pump blood around your body, and the lower number is the force of the blood as the heart relaxes between beats."

‌



"Now, if you're on medication for your blood pressure, it's important that you take it as prescribed. But here are some additional things that you can do to help keep your blood pressure at healthy levels."

He proceeded to detail and clarify five actions you can implement to maintain your blood pressure within a healthy range.

1. Eat less salt

"Number one, eat less salt," he said. "Now, if you don't have high blood pressure, then there's still a debate about how much salt will affect you. But if you do have high blood pressure, listen up."

‌



Dr Khan continued: "Adults should only have around six grams or one level teaspoon of salt per day. And most of that is already hidden in the food that we eat." Excessive salt intake is a leading cause of high blood pressure, as it disrupts the body's sodium balance, causing water retention and increased blood volume, which strains blood vessels.

"So, try not to add salt to your food," he added. "Instead, season it with things like pepper, herbs, and spices. And if you're buying tinned food, go for it in water rather than salty brine. And with nuts, always go for unsalted nuts."

2. Eat more potassium-rich foods

"Number two, eat more potassium-rich foods," Dr Khan advised before detailing: "Potassium helps lower blood pressure by helping kidneys get rid of that excess sodium or salt in your blood. Food that naturally contains potassium includes bananas, tomatoes, carrots, kiwi, nectarines, and spinach. If you have kidney disease, however, just be really careful with potassium."

‌



Potassium helps lower high blood pressure by easing tension in blood vessel walls and increasing sodium excretion through urine. A daily intake of 3,500–5,000 mg of potassium is recommended to manage blood pressure. High potassium intake significantly reduces stroke risk, but people with kidney disease should consult a doctor before increasing intake, according to the British Heart Foundation.

3. Exercise

"Number three, get moving," he urged. "Regular movement keeps your blood vessels flexible as they have to expand and contract and encourage blood flow around your body. Find something you enjoy doing and do it regularly."

The NHS recommends to do at least 150 minutes of exercise a week. This could include brisk walking, cycling, swimming, dancing, and gardening, according to the NHS, and should ideally be done in 30-minute sessions five days a week.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

4. Stop smoking and limit alcohol

Addressing the fourth item on his list, Dr Khan said: "Number four, stop smoking and limit alcohol use. Smoking can affect the health of your blood vessels, which causes high blood pressure, and alcohol is really strongly linked to high blood pressure too."

Smoking raises heart rate and blood pressure for 15–30 minutes per cigarette, while heavy or binge drinking causes both immediate spikes and long-term elevation in pressure, according to the NHS.

Article continues below

5. Keep a healthy weight

"And number five, achieve a healthy weight," he said. "I know this is hard and it's really complex but additional weight, especially around the middle area, has been linked to high blood pressure. These additional fat cells can release hormones that increase blood pressure.

"So follow the steps I outlined already to achieve good health alongside a healthy weight," he concluded in the video.

For those concerned about high blood pressure or who feel they may be at risk, the NHS advises booking an appointment with your GP. Alternatively, you can request a blood pressure check at your local pharmacy.

The quick actions of five middle school students may have prevented a disaster.

On Wednesday, a group of students from Hancock Middle School in Mississippi worked together after their school bus driver experienced a medical emergency and passed out.

Leah Taylor, the driver, told WLOX that the "students stepped up when I passed out driving the bus."

“She kind of fell over, like flopped over, and everyone started standing up,” McKenzy Finch, a sixth-grade, told the station.

Despite most of their driving experience likely being reserved to video games or four-wheelers, the students sprung into action and devised a genius way to stop the bus by working together.

open image in gallery Five middle school students, who helped stop a bus after their driver passed out during a medical emergency, stand outside a bus in Hancock County, Miss., on Thursday, April 23, 2026 ( AP )

With the vehicle still in motion, Jackson Casnave, who is also in sixth-grader, rushed to grab the bus's steering wheel.

“I saw that the bus was veering off to the side. Then, I grabbed the wheel,” he said. “It was just adrenaline pumping.”

Another classmate, Darius Clark, engaged the buses' air brake.

While those students worked to stop the bus, others attended to Taylor, with McKenzy and eighth-grader Destiny Cornelius administered aid to the driver.

Darius told the broadcaster that he had a harrowing experience with the air brakes.

“So, she passed out again, and then, the bus started rolling forward. It started gaining speed,” Darrius said. “I didn’t know it had air brakes, so when I clicked the brakes, it about threw me out the windshield.”

Once the boys has the bus under control, they parked it near a median and waited for help.

open image in gallery A Hancock County School District bus in Hancock County, Mississippi ( AP )

Destiny said she noticed that Taylor had been reaching for her medicine before she passed out.

“I saw her medication in her hand, and I saw her reaching for it. I knew that’s what she needed,” she told the broadcaster.

Taylor told reporters that she is feeling much better and is proud of the students on her bus.

“I’m very proud of them. I couldn’t ask for any better students than my students on my bus. I love every single one of them,” Taylor said. “I’m gonna think of how they saved my life.”

The school recognized the students with a pep rally. Melissa Saucier, the school's principal, said the students did exactly what was necessary to avoid injury or death.

“I’m not surprised to hear that our kids remained calm and acted swiftly,” Saucier said. “This emergency situation could have definitely been detrimental. They handled it exactly how they should have, and we’re extremely proud of them.”
